Okay! Imagine you have a special kind of toy car that looks really cool and old, but you don’t actually play with it every day. Instead, you look at it and maybe show it to your friends because it’s special.

Literary Latin is kind of like that special toy car. It’s the fancy, beautiful Latin that writers and poets used to write books, poems, and important speeches a long, long time ago—like when people like Julius Caesar or the writers of stories about gods and heroes.

But when regular people wanted to talk to each other—like at home, at the market, or with their friends—they didn’t use that fancy Latin. They used a different kind of Latin, the one they spoke every day, which was simpler and sounded different. This everyday Latin is called “Vulgar Latin.”

So, literary Latin was mostly for writing and reading, not for talking in everyday life. People didn’t use the fancy Latin when they were just chatting with each other.
